# kenji skills **You say the job. The playbook runs.** Agent skills, slash commands, and subagents for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and any agent that reads `SKILL.md`. 161 agent skills · 63 slash commands · 6 subagents · MCP templates. Written on React, Next.js, and Supabase projects; most of it works on any stack.

After you install, describe the job in chat. The matching playbook runs, checks its own result, and opens the PR.
## Quickstart You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18 or newer. Run these three commands: ```bash npx @kensaurus/skills --auto --dry-run # 1. preview: lists every file it would write, changes nothing npx @kensaurus/skills --auto # 2. install for each agent found on this machine npx @kensaurus/skills --auto --verify # 3. check every installed file against the package ``` `--auto` looks for `~/.cursor`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, and `~/.gemini` and installs for each one it finds. If it finds none, it installs for Cursor. To pick the tools yourself, use `--claude`, `--cursor`, `--codex`, `--gemini` (combine freely) or `--all`. Then restart your agent and describe a task in plain words, for example *"audit this repo for security problems"*. The [plain-language guide](docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) walks through a first session. > **Note:** the default install also adds an opt-in **Stop hook** to Claude Code and Cursor. It does nothing until you start a `complete-everything` or `burndown-full` run. To skip it, add `--only skills,commands,agents,rules`. Details: [The Stop hook](#the-stop-hook). ## Which agents are supported | Agent | Install with | Skills | Slash commands | Subagents | Rules | Stop hook | |:------|:-------------|:-------|:---------------|:----------|:------|:----------| | **Claude Code** | `--claude` | `~/.claude/skills/` | `~/.claude/commands/` | `~/.claude/agents/` | `~/.claude/rules/` (`.md`) | yes, in `~/.claude/settings.json` | | **Cursor** | bare command or `--cursor` | `~/.cursor/skills/`, plus a copy in `~/.agents/skills/` | `~/.cursor/commands/` | `~/.cursor/agents/` | `~/.cursor/rules/` (`.mdc`; see below) | yes, in `~/.cursor/hooks.json` | | **Codex CLI** | `--codex` | `~/.agents/skills/` | portable prompts in `~/.codex/prompts/` (see below) | no | merged into `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | no | | **Gemini CLI** | `--gemini` | `~/.agents/skills/` | portable commands in `~/.gemini/commands/` | no | merged into `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` | no | | **Any agent that reads `SKILL.md`** | `npx skills add kensaurus/skills` | that agent's skills folder | no | no | no | no | How each path was chosen: - **Codex CLI** reads user skills from `$HOME/.agents/skills` ([Codex skills docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills), "Where Codex loads local skills"). It reads global instructions from `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` ([AGENTS.md docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)). Codex has deprecated custom prompts ([custom prompts page](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/custom-prompts)), and a Codex maintainer says they were removed in codex-cli 0.117.0 ([openai/codex#15941](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15941)). The installer still writes the portable prompts for older Codex releases. On current Codex, use the skills. - **Gemini CLI** reads user skills from `~/.gemini/skills/` or the `~/.agents/skills/` alias. Within the user tier, the alias takes precedence ([Gemini CLI skills docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/), "Discovery tiers"). It reads global context from `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` ([GEMINI.md docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md)). - **Codex and Gemini share one copy in `~/.agents/skills/`.** It is written once per run, and other skills already in that folder are left alone, even by `--clean`. - With only `--codex` or `--gemini`, the installer writes just this pack's skill folders. - When Cursor is also a target, Cursor's mirror fills the folder instead, and the installer reuses that copy. The mirror copies everything in `~/.cursor/skills/`, so your own Cursor skills also become visible to Codex and Gemini. To avoid that, install Cursor in a separate run with `--no-agents-mirror`. - **Cursor** reads skills from `~/.cursor/skills/`. Its [rules docs](https://cursor.com/docs/rules) describe project rules in a repo's `.cursor/rules/` and user rules in Customize → Rules. They do not mention `~/.cursor/rules/`, where the installer puts the global rules. If a rule does not seem to apply in Cursor, copy the `.mdc` file into your project's `.cursor/rules/`. - **Claude Code** loads every file in `~/.claude/rules/` in every project, except rules with a `paths:` field, which load only when matching files are open ([Claude Code memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)). - **Other agents.** The [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) copies `SKILL.md` folders into the folder each agent reads, for example GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, or Antigravity CLI. Pass `-g` for your user folder and `-a ` for the agent. The IDs are in the skills CLI README under "Supported Agents". Example: `npx skills add kensaurus/skills -g -a github-copilot`. You get the skills in `skills/` only, without commands, subagents, rules, or the hook. - **Claude Code plugin.** Instead of the installer, you can run `/plugin marketplace add kensaurus/skills` and then `/plugin install kenji@kenji`. ## What the installer writes The installer is one Node script, [`bin/install.mjs`](bin/install.mjs). It has no dependencies or npm lifecycle scripts. It opens no network connection and starts no child processes; `npx` downloads the package before it runs. It writes only under your home directory: | Path | What | When it exists already | |:-----|:-----|:-----------------------| | `~/.cursor/skills//`, `~/.claude/skills//` | One folder per skill | Same-named files are overwritten. Your other skills stay. | | `~/.agents/skills//` | Skills for Codex and Gemini, and Cursor's mirror (which copies all of `~/.cursor/skills/`, yours included) | Same as above. Skip it with `--no-agents-mirror`, which also means Codex and Gemini get no skills. | | `~/.cursor/commands/`, `~/.claude/commands/` | Slash commands (`.md`) | Same-named files are overwritten. | | `~/.cursor/agents/`, `~/.claude/agents/` | Subagent definitions | Same-named files are overwritten. | | `~/.cursor/rules/`, `~/.claude/rules/` | Global rules (`.mdc` for Cursor, `.md` for Claude Code) | Same-named files are overwritten. | | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` | Global rules merged into one file | The old file is copied to `.bak-` first. An unchanged file is not rewritten. | | `~/.codex/prompts/*.md`, `~/.gemini/commands/*.toml` | `plan-mode`, `research`, `fix-issue` | Backed up like `AGENTS.md`. | | `~/.claude/kenji-hooks/`, `~/.cursor/kenji-hooks/` | `completion-gate.mjs`, the Stop hook script | Overwritten. | | `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.cursor/hooks.json` | One Stop hook entry | Merged. Your other settings and hooks are kept. A backup is written when the file changes. If the file is not valid JSON, the hook is skipped with a warning. | | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | MCP server template | Written only if missing. Never overwritten. | A normal run **merges**: it adds or overwrites this pack's files and never deletes your own. It also removes leftovers that this pack itself renamed or stopped installing. After every write, the installer hash-checks each copied file. **`--clean` is different.** It deletes the whole `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/`, and `rules/` folders under each targeted `~/.cursor` and `~/.claude`, **your own files in them included**, and then installs fresh. It first copies those folders to `/.kenji-backups//`, unless you pass `--no-backup`. It does not touch `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, or the Codex and Gemini command files. In `~/.agents/skills/` it removes only this pack's skill folders.
All installer flags ```bash npx @kensaurus/skills # Cursor only (the default) npx @kensaurus/skills --auto # every tool found under ~ (falls back to Cursor) npx @kensaurus/skills --all # Cursor + Claude Code + Codex CLI + Gemini CLI npx @kensaurus/skills --claude --codex # pick targets; combine freely npx @kensaurus/skills --only skills,commands # subset of: skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks npx @kensaurus/skills --skill audit-ux # one skill npx @kensaurus/skills --dry-run # preview, no writes npx @kensaurus/skills --verify # read-only hash check (add the same target flags) npx @kensaurus/skills --clean # delete skills/commands/agents/rules folders first, yours too (backed up) npx @kensaurus/skills --restore [stamp] # put a --clean backup back (latest if no stamp) npx @kensaurus/skills --link # symlink instead of copy, for editing skills in a clone npx @kensaurus/skills --no-agents-mirror # write nothing to ~/.agents/skills npx @kensaurus/skills --help # full help ``` From a clone, `./install.sh` with no arguments installs for Cursor and Claude Code. With arguments, it passes them to `node bin/install.mjs`.
### The Stop hook The completion gate, [`hooks/completion-gate.mjs`](hooks/completion-gate.mjs), is registered as a Stop hook in Claude Code and Cursor. It reads the open workspace for `.cursor/complete-everything-state.md` or `.cursor/burndown-state.md`. Those files exist only during a `complete-everything` or `burndown-full` run. If neither file exists, or the checklist was last updated more than a day ago, the hook exits without doing anything. Otherwise it sends the agent back to the unfinished items instead of letting it stop. After three follow-ups with no item closed, it gives up. Each run has a 5-second timeout and does not block the agent if it fails. - **Skip it at install time:** `npx @kensaurus/skills --all --only skills,commands,agents,rules`. Any `--only` also skips the `mcp.json` template. - **Remove it later:** delete the entry whose command contains `kenji-hooks/completion-gate.mjs` from `hooks.Stop` in `~/.claude/settings.json` and from `hooks.stop` in `~/.cursor/hooks.json`. Then delete `~/.claude/kenji-hooks/` and `~/.cursor/kenji-hooks/`. A later install without `--only` adds it back. ### The stack-specific parts, and how to skip them These skills and rules were written on React, Next.js, and Supabase projects. Here is what assumes that stack: | Piece | What it assumes | Loads when | |:------|:----------------|:-----------| | `rules/senior-engineer.mdc` | Next.js + React + Supabase defaults: TanStack Query, Zustand, Zod, RLS on every table | Claude Code: only with files under `app/`, `supabase/`, or `next.config.*` open (its `paths:` field). Cursor: when the agent judges its description relevant. Codex and Gemini: every session, because it is merged into `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md`. | | `rules/full-stack-ship-discipline.mdc` | Deploy schema with the feature; uses Supabase as the worked example | Claude Code, Codex, Gemini: every session (no `paths:` field). Cursor: when the agent judges its description relevant. | | `rules/project-starter/`, `rules/native-rn-monorepo/` | Per-project rule sets for Next.js/Supabase and React Native | Never installed. Copy them into a project yourself. | | Skills such as `plan-rls-audit`, `backend-realtime`, `mushi-*` | The tool in their name or description | Only when your request matches | The other global rules (`verification-before-completion`, `approved-plan-execution`, `shell-first-search`, `skill-workflows`) do not depend on a stack. To install without the global rules: `npx @kensaurus/skills --all --only skills,commands,agents`. This also skips the Stop hook and the MCP template. To drop a single rule, delete its file after installing. A later install without `--only` puts it back. ## Verify, update, uninstall **Verify.** `npx @kensaurus/skills --verify` plus the target flags you installed with (`--auto`, `--all`, `--codex`, …). It makes no changes. It fails if a packaged file is missing or differs from the package, and lists each one. Extra files of your own are allowed. Line endings are normalized before hashing, so CRLF copies on Windows still match. **Update.** Run the same install command again. Unchanged files are left as they are, and renamed skills from older releases are removed. **Roll back.** - `--clean` runs keep a backup. Restore it with `npx @kensaurus/skills --restore` (Cursor) or `--restore --claude`, plus a stamp from `.kenji-backups/` to pick an older one. - `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `settings.json`, `hooks.json`, and the Codex/Gemini command files keep `.bak-` copies next to them. Copy one back by hand. - A normal merge does **not** back up skill, command, agent, or rule files it overwrites. If you edited one of this pack's files in place, copy it somewhere first. **Uninstall.** There is no uninstall command. Remove the pieces by hand: ```bash # Skills, commands and agents this pack ships (bash; uses a fresh clone for the names) git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kensaurus/skills.git /tmp/kenji for d in /tmp/kenji/skills/*/ /tmp/kenji/skills-cursor/*/; do n=$(basename "$d"); rm -rf ~/.cursor/skills/"$n" ~/.claude/skills/"$n" ~/.agents/skills/"$n" done for f in /tmp/kenji/commands/*.md; do rm -f ~/.cursor/commands/"$(basename "$f")" ~/.claude/commands/"$(basename "$f")"; done for f in /tmp/kenji/agents/*.md; do rm -f ~/.cursor/agents/"$(basename "$f")" ~/.claude/agents/"$(basename "$f")"; done ``` Then remove what is left: - the global rules listed in [Rules](#commands-subagents-mcp-rules), from `~/.cursor/rules/` and `~/.claude/rules/`; - the Stop hook, as described in [The Stop hook](#the-stop-hook); - `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` (or restore a `.bak-` copy); - the `plan-mode`, `research`, and `fix-issue` files in `~/.codex/prompts/` and `~/.gemini/commands/`. Leave `~/.cursor/mcp.json` alone if you have edited it. To remove the Claude Code plugin, run `claude plugin uninstall kenji@kenji` ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#plugin-uninstall)). To remove skills installed by the skills CLI, run `npx skills remove`. ## Troubleshooting
Windows: EPERM or EBUSY during install Another program is holding a file, usually an open editor watching `~/.cursor` or `~/.claude`, or an antivirus scan. The installer retries each file for about 3 seconds, then stops and names the file. Close the editor and run the command again; a merge install is safe to repeat.
Windows: line endings (CRLF) `--verify` normalizes CRLF to LF before hashing text files, so a checkout made with `core.autocrlf=true` verifies cleanly. The repo's `.gitattributes` checks text files out with LF. If `./install.sh` still fails with `$'\r': command not found`, the script was checked out with CRLF line endings: clone again, or run `node bin/install.mjs` with the same arguments. `install.sh` needs bash (Git Bash or WSL); the Node installer does not.
"I already have skills, rules, or settings in those folders" A merge install keeps them. It only overwrites files with the same name as one of this pack's files. Run `--dry-run` first to see the exact list. Hook config files are merged entry by entry, and a backup is written when they change. To keep your own `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` instead of the merged one, install Codex or Gemini with `--only skills,commands` (or `--only skills`).
Codex shows only some skills, or shortened descriptions Codex lists skills within a budget: 2% of the model's context window, or 8,000 characters when the window is unknown. With many skills installed, it shortens descriptions first and may leave some skills out with a warning ([Codex skills docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills)). To install fewer skills, use `--codex --skill ` once per skill. To turn one off, add `[[skills.config]]` with `enabled = false` in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Claude Code has a similar listing budget; the installer prints its current size after a `--claude` install.
Codex: the /prompts: commands are missing Current Codex releases no longer load `~/.codex/prompts/` (see the links in [Which agents are supported](#which-agents-are-supported)). Use the skills instead: type `$` or run `/skills`.
Codex: I set CODEX_HOME The installer always writes `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and `~/.codex/prompts/`. Copy them into your `CODEX_HOME`. Codex reads `AGENTS.override.md` instead of `AGENTS.md` when that file exists, so check for one. Skills are not affected; Codex reads `$HOME/.agents/skills` either way.
Gemini CLI asks before a skill runs That is how Gemini CLI works: activating a skill asks for consent and grants the skill's folder read access ([docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/)). In a running session, `/skills reload` picks up new skills and `/memory reload` re-reads `GEMINI.md`. The same page says Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI for unpaid-tier and Google One users on June 18, 2026. This installer does not target Antigravity CLI. The skills CLI lists an `antigravity-cli` agent ID.
A skill does not trigger Skills are matched against what you say. Name the skill to force it, for example *"use `audit-security` on this repo"*, or call it directly: `/audit-security` in Claude Code and Cursor, `$audit-security` in Codex. Trigger phrases for every skill: [docs/CATALOG.md](docs/CATALOG.md).
## How one request lifts the repo Every playbook follows the same five steps. It assesses before it changes anything, and proves the result before it ships. | Rung | What runs | What the repo gains | |:-----|:----------|:--------------------| | **Orient** | `workflow-onboard`, `/research` | A decision log | | **Assess** | `audit-*`, `plan-*`, `/grill-me` | A failing test, or a plan you approve | | **Change** | `design-*`, `enhance-*`, `backend-*`, `housekeep-*` | A diff you can read in one sitting | | **Prove** | `test-*`, `complete-everything`, `completion-judge` | Evidence, not a claim | | **Ship** | `workflow-ship-and-observe`, `deploy-*`, `debug-*` | A release that stayed up | The 23 `plan-*` skills audit first and wait for your approval. See [docs/PLAN-LOOPS.md](docs/PLAN-LOOPS.md). ## What should I say? | You say… | What kicks in | What you get | |:---------|:--------------|:-------------| | *"orient me"* | `workflow-onboard` | A short tour of the codebase | | *"grill me before I build"* | `workflow-grilling` | One question at a time until you're aligned | | *"build this feature"* | `workflow-build-feature` | Spec → tests → code → smoke → PR | | *"fix this bug and ship it"* | `workflow-fix-and-ship` | Debug → fix → verify → PR → deploy | | *"this mobile app feels like a website"* | `enhance-mobile-native-feel` | Native chrome, haptics, motion, lists, in one pass | | *"fix our mobile UI/UX end to end"* | `workflow-mobile-native-uiux` | Native pass → accessibility → device QA → PR | | *"audit my security"* | `audit-security` | OWASP-style findings with file:line | | *"is this production-ready?"* | `audit-resilience` + `audit-realworld` | Timeouts, retries, parity checks | | *"complete everything"* | `complete-everything` | No parked leftovers; a judge verifies "done" | | *"ship it and watch it"* | `workflow-ship-and-observe` | Deploy → verify live → observe / rollback | | *"take this to market"* | `workflow-gtm` | GTM plan → approve → analytics, hero, onboarding, SEO, launch kit | To force a skill: *"use `enhance-web-ux` on `/dashboard`"*. Every trigger phrase → [docs/CATALOG.md](docs/CATALOG.md). ## Tour Four examples. Each time, you describe the job and a named playbook runs.

Grill · workflow-grilling asks one question at a time. You approve a decision log before any code.
Build · workflow-build-feature writes the spec and the failing test first. Then the code, then the PR.

Audit · audit-security reports each finding with a file and line.
Ship · workflow-ship-and-observe confirms the live revision, watches the window, and rolls back if it breaks.

161 agent skills · 63 slash commands · 6 subagents · MCP templates. Written on React, Next.js, and Supabase projects; most of it works on any stack.

<p>

<sub>After you install, describe the job in chat. The matching playbook runs, checks its own result, and opens the PR.</sub>

</div>

<img src="docs/screenshots/icons/install.png" width="28" height="28" alt="" align="absmiddle"> Quickstart

You need Node.js 18 or newer. Run these three commands:


npx @kensaurus/skills --auto --dry-run   # 1. preview: lists every file it would write, changes nothing

npx @kensaurus/skills --auto             # 2. install for each agent found on this machine

npx @kensaurus/skills --auto --verify    # 3. check every installed file against the package

--auto looks for ~/.cursor, ~/.claude, ~/.codex, and ~/.gemini and installs for each one it finds. If it finds none, it installs for Cursor. To pick the tools yourself, use --claude, --cursor, --codex, --gemini (combine freely) or --all.

Then restart your agent and describe a task in plain words, for example *"audit this repo for security problems"*. The [plain-language guide](docs/GETTING-STARTED.md) walks through a first session.

> Note: the default install also adds an opt-in Stop hook to Claude Code and Cursor. It does nothing until you start a complete-everything or burndown-full run. To skip it, add --only skills,commands,agents,rules. Details: [The Stop hook](#the-stop-hook).

<img src="docs/screenshots/icons/options.png" width="28" height="28" alt="" align="absmiddle"> Which agents are supported

| Agent | Install with | Skills | Slash commands | Subagents | Rules | Stop hook |

|:------|:-------------|:-------|:---------------|:----------|:------|:----------|

| Claude Code | --claude | ~/.claude/skills/ | ~/.claude/commands/ | ~/.claude/agents/ | ~/.claude/rules/ (.md) | yes, in ~/.claude/settings.json |

| Cursor | bare command or --cursor | ~/.cursor/skills/, plus a copy in ~/.agents/skills/ | ~/.cursor/commands/ | ~/.cursor/agents/ | ~/.cursor/rules/ (.mdc; see below) | yes, in ~/.cursor/hooks.json |

| Codex CLI | --codex | ~/.agents/skills/ | portable prompts in ~/.codex/prompts/ (see below) | no | merged into ~/.codex/AGENTS.md | no |

| Gemini CLI | --gemini | ~/.agents/skills/ | portable commands in ~/.gemini/commands/ | no | merged into ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md | no |

| Any agent that reads SKILL.md | npx skills add kensaurus/skills | that agent's skills folder | no | no | no | no |

How each path was chosen:

  • Codex CLI reads user skills from $HOME/.agents/skills (Codex skills docs, "Where Codex loads local skills"). It reads global instructions from ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (AGENTS.md docs). Codex has deprecated custom prompts (custom prompts page), and a Codex maintainer says they were removed in codex-cli 0.117.0 (openai/codex#15941). The installer still writes the portable prompts for older Codex releases. On current Codex, use the skills.
  • Gemini CLI reads user skills from ~/.gemini/skills/ or the ~/.agents/skills/ alias. Within the user tier, the alias takes precedence (Gemini CLI skills docs, "Discovery tiers"). It reads global context from ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md (GEMINI.md docs).
  • Codex and Gemini share one copy in ~/.agents/skills/. It is written once per run, and other skills already in that folder are left alone, even by --clean.

- With only --codex or --gemini, the installer writes just this pack's skill folders.

- When Cursor is also a target, Cursor's mirror fills the folder instead, and the installer reuses that copy. The mirror copies everything in ~/.cursor/skills/, so your own Cursor skills also become visible to Codex and Gemini. To avoid that, install Cursor in a separate run with --no-agents-mirror.

  • Cursor reads skills from ~/.cursor/skills/. Its rules docs describe project rules in a repo's .cursor/rules/ and user rules in Customize → Rules. They do not mention ~/.cursor/rules/, where the installer puts the global rules. If a rule does not seem to apply in Cursor, copy the .mdc file into your project's .cursor/rules/.
  • Claude Code loads every file in ~/.claude/rules/ in every project, except rules with a paths: field, which load only when matching files are open (Claude Code memory docs).
  • Other agents. The skills CLI copies SKILL.md folders into the folder each agent reads, for example GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, or Antigravity CLI. Pass -g for your user folder and -a <agent-id> for the agent. The IDs are in the skills CLI README under "Supported Agents". Example: npx skills add kensaurus/skills -g -a github-copilot. You get the skills in skills/ only, without commands, subagents, rules, or the hook.
  • Claude Code plugin. Instead of the installer, you can run /plugin marketplace add kensaurus/skills and then /plugin install kenji@kenji.

<picture>

<source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/screenshots/architecture-dark.png">

<source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="docs/screenshots/architecture-light.png">

<img alt="Diagram: skills, commands, subagents, rules, and MCP templates go through npx @kensaurus/skills --all into ~/.cursor and ~/.claude (skills, commands, agents, rules), ~/.codex (AGENTS.md and prompts, plus skills in ~/.agents) and ~/.gemini (GEMINI.md and commands, plus skills in ~/.agents)." src="docs/screenshots/architecture-dark.png" width="100%">

</picture>

What the installer writes

The installer is one Node script, [bin/install.mjs](bin/install.mjs). It has no dependencies or npm lifecycle scripts. It opens no network connection and starts no child processes; npx downloads the package before it runs. It writes only under your home directory:

| Path | What | When it exists already |

|:-----|:-----|:-----------------------|

| ~/.cursor/skills/<name>/, ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ | One folder per skill | Same-named files are overwritten. Your other skills stay. |

| ~/.agents/skills/<name>/ | Skills for Codex and Gemini, and Cursor's mirror (which copies all of ~/.cursor/skills/, yours included) | Same as above. Skip it with --no-agents-mirror, which also means Codex and Gemini get no skills. |

| ~/.cursor/commands/, ~/.claude/commands/ | Slash commands (.md) | Same-named files are overwritten. |

| ~/.cursor/agents/, ~/.claude/agents/ | Subagent definitions | Same-named files are overwritten. |

| ~/.cursor/rules/, ~/.claude/rules/ | Global rules (.mdc for Cursor, .md for Claude Code) | Same-named files are overwritten. |

| ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md | Global rules merged into one file | The old file is copied to <file>.bak-<timestamp> first. An unchanged file is not rewritten. |

| ~/.codex/prompts/*.md, ~/.gemini/commands/*.toml | plan-mode, research, fix-issue | Backed up like AGENTS.md. |

| ~/.claude/kenji-hooks/, ~/.cursor/kenji-hooks/ | completion-gate.mjs, the Stop hook script | Overwritten. |

| ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.cursor/hooks.json | One Stop hook entry | Merged. Your other settings and hooks are kept. A backup is written when the file changes. If the file is not valid JSON, the hook is skipped with a warning. |

| ~/.cursor/mcp.json | MCP server template | Written only if missing. Never overwritten. |

A normal run merges: it adds or overwrites this pack's files and never deletes your own. It also removes leftovers that this pack itself renamed or stopped installing. After every write, the installer hash-checks each copied file.

--clean is different. It deletes the whole skills/, commands/, agents/, and rules/ folders under each targeted ~/.cursor and ~/.claude, your own files in them included, and then installs fresh. It first copies those folders to <base>/.kenji-backups/<timestamp>/, unless you pass --no-backup. It does not touch AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, or the Codex and Gemini command files. In ~/.agents/skills/ it removes only this pack's skill folders.

<details>

<summary><b>All installer flags</b></summary>


npx @kensaurus/skills                   # Cursor only (the default)

npx @kensaurus/skills --auto            # every tool found under ~ (falls back to Cursor)

npx @kensaurus/skills --all             # Cursor + Claude Code + Codex CLI + Gemini CLI

npx @kensaurus/skills --claude --codex  # pick targets; combine freely

npx @kensaurus/skills --only skills,commands      # subset of: skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks

npx @kensaurus/skills --skill audit-ux  # one skill

npx @kensaurus/skills --dry-run         # preview, no writes

npx @kensaurus/skills --verify          # read-only hash check (add the same target flags)

npx @kensaurus/skills --clean           # delete skills/commands/agents/rules folders first, yours too (backed up)

npx @kensaurus/skills --restore [stamp] # put a --clean backup back (latest if no stamp)

npx @kensaurus/skills --link            # symlink instead of copy, for editing skills in a clone

npx @kensaurus/skills --no-agents-mirror  # write nothing to ~/.agents/skills

npx @kensaurus/skills --help            # full help

From a clone, ./install.sh with no arguments installs for Cursor and Claude Code. With arguments, it passes them to node bin/install.mjs.

</details>

The Stop hook

The completion gate, [hooks/completion-gate.mjs](hooks/completion-gate.mjs), is registered as a Stop hook in Claude Code and Cursor. It reads the open workspace for .cursor/complete-everything-state.md or .cursor/burndown-state.md. Those files exist only during a complete-everything or burndown-full run. If neither file exists, or the checklist was last updated more than a day ago, the hook exits without doing anything. Otherwise it sends the agent back to the unfinished items instead of letting it stop. After three follow-ups with no item closed, it gives up. Each run has a 5-second timeout and does not block the agent if it fails.

  • Skip it at install time: npx @kensaurus/skills --all --only skills,commands,agents,rules. Any --only also skips the mcp.json template.
  • Remove it later: delete the entry whose command contains kenji-hooks/completion-gate.mjs from hooks.Stop in ~/.claude/settings.json and from hooks.stop in ~/.cursor/hooks.json. Then delete ~/.claude/kenji-hooks/ and ~/.cursor/kenji-hooks/. A later install without --only adds it back.

The stack-specific parts, and how to skip them

These skills and rules were written on React, Next.js, and Supabase projects. Here is what assumes that stack:

| Piece | What it assumes | Loads when |

|:------|:----------------|:-----------|

| rules/senior-engineer.mdc | Next.js + React + Supabase defaults: TanStack Query, Zustand, Zod, RLS on every table | Claude Code: only with files under app/, supabase/, or next.config.* open (its paths: field). Cursor: when the agent judges its description relevant. Codex and Gemini: every session, because it is merged into AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md. |

| rules/full-stack-ship-discipline.mdc | Deploy schema with the feature; uses Supabase as the worked example | Claude Code, Codex, Gemini: every session (no paths: field). Cursor: when the agent judges its description relevant. |

| rules/project-starter/, rules/native-rn-monorepo/ | Per-project rule sets for Next.js/Supabase and React Native | Never installed. Copy them into a project yourself. |

| Skills such as plan-rls-audit, backend-realtime, mushi-* | The tool in their name or description | Only when your request matches |

The other global rules (verification-before-completion, approved-plan-execution, shell-first-search, skill-workflows) do not depend on a stack.

To install without the global rules: npx @kensaurus/skills --all --only skills,commands,agents. This also skips the Stop hook and the MCP template. To drop a single rule, delete its file after installing. A later install without --only puts it back.

<img src="docs/screenshots/icons/upgrade.png" width="28" height="28" alt="" align="absmiddle"> Verify, update, uninstall

Verify. npx @kensaurus/skills --verify plus the target flags you installed with (--auto, --all, --codex, …). It makes no changes. It fails if a packaged file is missing or differs from the package, and lists each one. Extra files of your own are allowed. Line endings are normalized before hashing, so CRLF copies on Windows still match.

Update. Run the same install command again. Unchanged files are left as they are, and renamed skills from older releases are removed.

Roll back.

  • --clean runs keep a backup. Restore it with npx @kensaurus/skills --restore (Cursor) or --restore --claude, plus a stamp from .kenji-backups/ to pick an older one.
  • AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, settings.json, hooks.json, and the Codex/Gemini command files keep .bak-<timestamp> copies next to them. Copy one back by hand.
  • A normal merge does not back up skill, command, agent, or rule files it overwrites. If you edited one of this pack's files in place, copy it somewhere first.

Uninstall. There is no uninstall command. Remove the pieces by hand:


# Skills, commands and agents this pack ships (bash; uses a fresh clone for the names)

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kensaurus/skills.git /tmp/kenji

for d in /tmp/kenji/skills/*/ /tmp/kenji/skills-cursor/*/; do

  n=$(basename "$d"); rm -rf ~/.cursor/skills/"$n" ~/.claude/skills/"$n" ~/.agents/skills/"$n"

done

for f in /tmp/kenji/commands/*.md; do rm -f ~/.cursor/commands/"$(basename "$f")" ~/.claude/commands/"$(basename "$f")"; done

for f in /tmp/kenji/agents/*.md;   do rm -f ~/.cursor/agents/"$(basename "$f")"   ~/.claude/agents/"$(basename "$f")"; done

Then remove what is left:

  • the global rules listed in [Rules](#commands-subagents-mcp-rules), from ~/.cursor/rules/ and ~/.claude/rules/;
  • the Stop hook, as described in [The Stop hook](#the-stop-hook);
  • ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md (or restore a .bak- copy);
  • the plan-mode, research, and fix-issue files in ~/.codex/prompts/ and ~/.gemini/commands/.

Leave ~/.cursor/mcp.json alone if you have edited it. To remove the Claude Code plugin, run claude plugin uninstall kenji@kenji (docs). To remove skills installed by the skills CLI, run npx skills remove.

Troubleshooting

<details>

<summary><b>Windows: <code>EPERM</code> or <code>EBUSY</code> during install</b></summary>

Another program is holding a file, usually an open editor watching ~/.cursor or ~/.claude, or an antivirus scan. The installer retries each file for about 3 seconds, then stops and names the file. Close the editor and run the command again; a merge install is safe to repeat.

</details>

<details>

<summary><b>Windows: line endings (CRLF)</b></summary>

--verify normalizes CRLF to LF before hashing text files, so a checkout made with core.autocrlf=true verifies cleanly. The repo's .gitattributes checks text files out with LF. If ./install.sh still fails with $'\r': command not found, the script was checked out with CRLF line endings: clone again, or run node bin/install.mjs with the same arguments. install.sh needs bash (Git Bash or WSL); the Node installer does not.

</details>

<details>

<summary><b>"I already have skills, rules, or settings in those folders"</b></summary>

A merge install keeps them. It only overwrites files with the same name as one of this pack's files. Run --dry-run first to see the exact list. Hook config files are merged entry by entry, and a backup is written when they change. To keep your own AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md instead of the merged one, install Codex or Gemini with --only skills,commands (or --only skills).

</details>

<details>

<summary><b>Codex shows only some skills, or shortened descriptions</b></summary>

Codex lists skills within a budget: 2% of the model's context window, or 8,000 characters when the window is unknown. With many skills installed, it shortens descriptions first and may leave some skills out with a warning (Codex skills docs). To install fewer skills, use --codex --skill <name> once per skill.
